name: Politecnico di Torino
summary: Turin's technical university; six engineering and architecture bachelor's taught fully in English, entered by the TIL test or (engineering) the SAT.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma: 24+ points, 12 of them at HL, and TOK, EE and CAS passed. An IB studied wholly in English proves your English (B2 needed). Every degree needs the TIL test or SAT.

programmes.name: Architecture (English-taught)
programmes.about: Architectural design for better places to live: designing simple civic buildings, surveying modern and historic buildings, and working on projects from concept to construction.
programmes.ib: National TIL-A test in person in Turin, sat in English; SAT not accepted. 2026: register 12 June–15 July, test 21 or 22 July.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on the TIL-A test. Up to 40 of the EU places are for the English-taught programme. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: register 12 June–15 July; TIL-A 21 or 22 July

programmes.name: Automotive Engineering (entirely in English)
programmes.about: The motor vehicle as a system: its main sub-systems and how it is produced, for designing automotive components in teams; home of a long-running Formula SAE student team.
programmes.ib: TIL-I test (in English or Italian) or SAT with 650+ in each section. Places are shared with the Italian track (214 in all, 174 for EU students).
programmes.selectionNote: TIL-I score of 60/100 guarantees your first choice; from 30/100 or a valid SAT you enter the merit ranking. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: TIL sessions 19 Feb–4 May; EU-only session 15 July

notes: The TIL test is sat in person in Turin, in several sessions from February; later sessions run only while places remain, and the last one is for EU and equivalent applicants only.
The 2027-28 calls are not published yet; the 2026-27 calls came out in December 2025, test registration opening in January.
Automotive, Computer and Mechanical Engineering also run in Italian; you choose the English track when you register.
